clue.text: Hun is able to carry petrol

definitions.note: a phrase of purpose standing for the container that does it

blocks.note: Jerry and Hun were both wartime British slang for a German
to be able is to can

explanation.surface: A German soldier is perfectly capable of hauling fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a jerrycan is the flat-sided steel container made to carry petrol, first copied from German army cans.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerrycan is a standard steel fuel container, so describing it by its purpose of transporting fuel works as a looser descriptive definition.

clue.text: Queries complicated title

indicators.note: complicated means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: Questions arise about an intricate form of address.
explanation.definitionFit: Esquire, or Esq., is a courtesy title written after a gentleman's name on letters.

clue.text: What drivers need to be aware of when following the route

blocks.note: a road is a route
to sense something is to be aware of it

explanation.surface: Reads as straightforward advice for motorists on staying alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When following' puts the awareness word after the route word.
explanation.definitionFit: Road sense is the instinct for safe behaviour in traffic that motorists, cyclists and pedestrians require.

clue.text: Some soldiers take care of king in dangerous surroundings

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other

blocks.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
a hot situation is a dangerous one; it surrounds the next piece
R is Rex, king

explanation.surface: Troops looking after their king amid peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort was a tenth of a Roman legion, a body of fighting men.

clue.text: These singers troubled and upset by myopia

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are shaken into a new order
upset means knocked over, a second signal that the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the main fodder
the rest of the fodder

explanation.surface: A choir that cannot read the music because their eyesight is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' sits between the two signals but is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is the medical term for being unable to see distant things clearly.

clue.text: Fixed ready for hanging

blocks.note: first meaning: rigged so an innocent person is blamed
second meaning: put in a mount, as a picture is before it goes on a wall

explanation.surface: Sounds like a stitched-up prisoner awaiting the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests execution, which fits 'fixed' as a stitch-up; the second sense is a picture hung on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A person set up falsely has been rigged against, and a picture placed in a border is ready to be hung.

clue.text: Dramatist - not Archer, though he may have worked for him

definitions.text: he may have worked for him

blocks.note: first meaning: John ..., Jacobean playwright who collaborated with Beaumont and Shakespeare

blocks.clueFragment: he may have worked for him
blocks.note: second meaning: a maker of arrows, who would supply a bowman

explanation.surface: Says the playwright is not Jeffrey Archer, though maybe his assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archer' suggests the novelist Jeffrey Archer, who also wrote plays; read as a bowman, he is the customer of an arrow-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: John Fletcher wrote plays with Beaumont, and a fletcher is a craftsman who makes arrows for bowmen.

clue.text: Can European dancers go round it?

definitions.text: Can European dancers go round it?

blocks.note: may and can both express permission
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A question whether dancers from the continent may circle something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: folk dancers circle it on May Day holding ribbons.
explanation.definitionFit: A maypole is the tall decorated post round which dancers weave ribbons in spring celebrations.

clue.text: Raised (what nonsense!) a well-known cap

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: rot is nonsense
taken as written
noted means famous

explanation.surface: Someone doffing a famous hat, with an outburst of disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole sequence is flipped upwards, as the clue is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion cap is a small explosive charge that sets off a larger one, which is what a detonator does.

clue.text: Press for a game

blocks.note: first meaning: crush or flatten
second meaning: a racket sport played against a walled court

explanation.surface: Like lobbying the newspapers to cover a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatten something by squeezing is one sense; the other is the indoor racket sport played off four walls.

clue.text: You can't get stoned with this stone

definitions.text: You can't get stoned with this stone

blocks.note: surface reading: a joke about drugs or about being pelted with rocks
setter's reading: a purple gem whose Greek name means not drunk, worn as a charm against intoxication

explanation.walkthrough: The Greeks believed this violet quartz kept its wearer sober; its name means 'not intoxicated', so 'stoned' is the slang for drunk or high.
explanation.definitionFit: The gem is a purple variety of quartz, and ancient lore held that it prevented drunkenness, which the clue's joke rests on.

clue.text: Chinks shoot around American ship retreating south

indicators.note: something retreating goes backwards, so the letters run the other way
one thing set around another encloses it

blocks.note: to fire a gun is to shoot it
USS, United States Ship, prefixes American naval vessels
S is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: Sounds like a naval engagement in which gunfire surrounds a US vessel heading south.
explanation.definitionFit: A chink is a narrow crack or opening, the same thing as a fissure in rock or a wall.

clue.text: Clown takes on protective covering

blocks.note: Coco was a famous circus clown
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clown puts on a costume for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown, Nicolai Poliakoff, was Britain's best-known circus clown; 'takes' just joins him to ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is the silky case a caterpillar spins round itself as shelter while it changes.

clue.text: Make a false move, sounding not very bright

indicators.note: sounding tells us to go by how the following words are pronounced

blocks.note: a dim light is faint

explanation.surface: Advice to a dim-witted boxer about a dummy punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A feint is a pretended attack meant to deceive an opponent, the deceptive move of boxing and fencing.

clue.text: Turn into the wind getting up around starboard side? Shocking!

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means the letters climb, read upwards
around places one piece about another, enclosing it

blocks.note: to luff is to steer a sailing boat closer to the wind
starboard is the right-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A sailing manoeuvre gone alarmingly wrong as the breeze rises.
explanation.walkthrough: LUFF is a sailing term; reversed it encloses the starboard word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frightful is dreadful or appalling, which is what shocking means as an exclamation.

clue.text: Enter game, making contract

indicators.note: game here is an adjective for willing to play along, so the letters are up for rearranging

blocks.note: the first part of the fodder
the second part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Joining a sport after signing terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are fodder; there is no separate indicator beyond 'making', which signals the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a formal binding arrangement between parties, which is what an agreement is.

clue.text: Chap with a name for abuse

blocks.note: a chap is a man
a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: Someone notorious for mistreatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle is to treat roughly or push about, a form of physical mistreatment.

clue.text: Rustic the majority often left to the devil

blocks.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer
most is the greater part

explanation.surface: Country folk, mostly abandoned to Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the saying 'Every man for himself, and the devil take the hindmost'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying lets the devil seize whoever falls last, so the last in line is the one abandoned to him.

clue.text: I am to act as a go-between, without delay

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for an adjective; 'immediate action' is action without delay

blocks.note: I am shortens to I'm
to mediate is to negotiate between two sides

explanation.surface: Someone volunteering to step in at once as a negotiator.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immediate happens at once, instantly, with no interval or pause before it.

clue.text: Messenger in his element

blocks.note: first meaning: the winged Roman god who carried messages
second meaning: the liquid metal, Hg

explanation.surface: A courier entirely at ease in his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In his element' is the idiom for comfortable; here 'element' is chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman messenger of the gods shares his name with the silvery metal used in thermometers.

clue.text: Short of two articles from abroad

blocks.note: un is French for a
der is German for the

explanation.surface: A writer lacking a couple of foreign pieces for a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' are grammatical: one French indefinite article and one German definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Being below a number is falling short of it, as in under ten pounds.

clue.text: Dodge gets 90 in bar

indicators.note: here gets means takes in, one word receiving another inside it

blocks.note: to elude is to dodge
XC is 90 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cricketer who swerves to score ninety in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to keep them out, the same as excluding them.

clue.text: The business of plaiting raffia

indicators.note: plaiting weaves strands over one another, so the letters are interwoven anew

blocks.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: A craft trade in weaving palm fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can mean a matter or concern, as in 'that is my affair', which is one's business.

clue.text: It was one in the eye for him

definitions.text: It was one in the eye for him

blocks.note: surface reading: an idiom for a humiliating setback
setter's reading: the English king traditionally killed at Hastings in 1066 by an arrow in the eye

explanation.walkthrough: The Bayeux Tapestry is read as showing the last Anglo-Saxon king struck in the eye by a Norman arrow; the idiom is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The king who lost the Battle of Hastings is said to have been shot through the eye, so the idiom fits him literally.

clue.text: Intended as follow-up of foreign challenge

blocks.note: de is French for of
one's intended is the person one is engaged to

explanation.surface: A betrothed arriving after someone foreign, inviting a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As follow-up of' puts the intended after the foreign word for 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance or a bold dare to authority, which is what a challenge offers.

clue.text: By the sound of it, in favour of a little golf

indicators.note: these words ask us to judge by ear rather than by spelling

blocks.note: being in favour of something is being for it, and a little of it is some

explanation.surface: Someone saying they are keen on a short round on the links.
explanation.walkthrough: A foursome is a golf match between two pairs; 'a little' is wordplay, and 'golf' alone names the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf match played by two pairs of partners is called by this name, a common social format of the game.

clue.text: Film street misses the point of passion

indicators.note: missing something means going without it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: Wardour Street in Soho is the traditional home of the British film industry
W, west, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A cinema-district road lacking purpose, or the reason for fervour.
explanation.walkthrough: Wardour Street is the London street long associated with film distributors; dropping its first letter, a compass point, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense enthusiasm or warmth of feeling, a close synonym of passion.

clue.text: Fell design

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb phrase, to knock someone flat
second meaning: as a noun, the arrangement of a page or plan

explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints the count as (3-3): LAY OUT as two words is knocking someone down, the hyphenated noun is a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay someone out is to floor them with a blow, and a page's arrangement is its plan or design.

clue.text: His spelling is usually bad

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who cannot spell words correctly
setter's reading: casting magic spells, usually evil ones, as a wizard does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelling' means casting spells, and 'bad' means wicked rather than inaccurate.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard who practises black magic casts spells that are typically malevolent.
